headline: Two parties want the nitrogen law delayed after a university's calculation error
headline_short: Parties seek delay to nitrogen law
deck: Aarhus University has apologised for the mistake; the minister says it must be put right.
standard: Venstre, a liberal party, and Liberal Alliance, a libertarian party, want the nitrogen law delayed by half a year after Aarhus University admitted errors in the calculations behind the law's discharge limits. The law is due to take effect after new year.

The university announced the error on Tuesday, having said the previous week that it had double-checked its figures after criticism from Seges, agriculture's think tank. Because of the error, some farmers would have been allowed to discharge less nitrogen than they should.
Christian Rabjerg Madsen, the minister for nature and animal welfare, told Ritzau in a written comment: 'I take that very seriously, and it must of course be put right.'
short: Venstre, a liberal party, and Liberal Alliance, a libertarian party, want the nitrogen law delayed by half a year after Aarhus University admitted errors in the calculations behind its limits on farmers' nitrogen discharges.
